newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian banks rally amid rate cut speculation.
newsitem.headline: Canadian banks rally amid rate cut speculation.

text.p: Canadian bank stocks soared to new heights on Friday, spurred by market speculation that Canadian interest rates may drop again next week.
Shares in the so-called Big Six banks hit 52-week highs on the Toronto Stock Exchange, extending their strong rally of recent months.

Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce led the charge, up 1.20 at 54.70 in afternoon turnover of 700,000 shares. The stock earlier reached a 52-week peak of 54.80. "A lot of people are looking for lower rates in Canada in the near term even if nothing happens south of the border," a trader said.
The Bank of Canada did not fulfil market expectations that it would cut its key bank rate early this morning. But analysts said they expected a move as early as next week.
The Bank of Canada last cut rates on October 2, dropping its key bank rate to 4.0 percent, which prompted Canada's chartered banks to lower their prime lending rates.
Declining interest rates make bank lending more profitable and bank dividends more attractive for investors.
Among the other banks, Royal Bank of Canada rose 0.65 to a 52-week high of 41.50. Bank of Montreal gained 0.95 to 39.40 after a peak of 39.50.
Bank of Nova Scotia improved 0.90 to a 52-week high of 40.95.
Toronto-Dominion Bank gained 0.30 to 30.20 after earlier reaching a 52-week high of 30.45. National Bank of Canada climbed 0.20 to 12.75, a 52-week peak.
